observations.statement: The 2021 Foodinho record identifies rating-linked opportunity, exclusion risk, and missing human-intervention and contestation procedures.
The Deliveroo record identifies intensive geolocation, assignment and shift-booking systems, and required substantive human intervention and periodic checks.
A later Deliveroo measure preserves formal follow-up custody without proving worker-level repair.
The 2024 Foodinho record shows renewed regulatory scrutiny and company-reported changes to biometric retention.
Repeated enforcement makes recurrence and drift addressable but does not prove that the same configuration persisted unchanged.
Named rider restoration, compensation, independent model validation, and survivor-bias reconciliation remain unrecovered.

open_questions: Was the correction implemented at the operative system boundary?
Were affected records, access, pay, duties, or accounts restored?
Was implementation independently verified after the deadline?
Did exits, silence, deterrence, overturns, restoration, and compensation enter later validation?
title: Foodinho, Glovo, and Deliveroo: repeated enforcement versus durable algorithmic learning
